answer.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation down 6%, directly matching the domains of memory_31 and memory_86, both of which report durable, unambiguous lifts from simplifying/shortening onboarding with no noted retention harm. This is a safer bet than promotional_pricing, which memory_73 explicitly warns caused strong acquisition/revenue lift but materially damaged 30-day retention — a direct threat to the stated objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, even though competitor pricing pressure makes it tempting. Referral incentives and enterprise sales-assist are solid but don't address this quarter's specific regressions. Activation messaging (memory_91) is a plausible alternative but onboarding sits earlier in the funnel and may be the root cause of the activation dip, so fixing it could compound benefits. I verify memory_86 and memory_31 since the entire choice rests on their evidence quality being as strong as summarized before committing the week's single experiment slot. Scale is kept to a standard experiment rather than broad rollout since even well-supported memories are consolidated summaries that could omit context (segment differences, time decay, interaction with current competitive dynamics), so I don't treat them as guaranteed to generalize to current conditions.
